articles.title: Joao Fonseca dice adiós al US Open
articles.standfirst: El brasileño continúa con su recuperación del abdominal y no disputará el último grande del año
articles.summary: El brasileño continúa con su recuperación del abdominal y no disputará el último grande del año
articles.body: Tras las recientes bajas de Jannik Sinner y Jack Draper, el nombre de Joao Fonseca se une a la lista. El tenista brasileño continúa con la recuperación de la lesión abdominal y se ha visto obligado a bajarse del US Open 2026. “Hola a todos. Quería darles una actualización. Después de someterme a pruebas y empezar un tratamiento en el abdomen, nos ha quedado claro a mi equipo y a mí que necesito más tiempo para recuperarme y poder competir de nuevo al más alto nivel. Desafortunadamente, eso significa que no podré estar en el US Open. No ha sido una decisión fácil de tomar, ya que es un torneo muy especial para mí. Seguiremos trabajando para poder volver lo antes posible. Agradezco inmensamente todos los mensajes de apoyo y todas las felicitaciones de cumpleaños. ¡Muchas gracias!”, fue el mensaje que publicó el brasileño en sus redes sociales. Al igual que en el Masters 1000 de Cincinnati, donde tuvo que abandonar en la tercera ronda del torneo ante el australiano Christopher O'Connell, el abdomen no le da tregua al actual número 26 del mundo y terminará la gira americana de pista rápida con cuatro partidos disputados (tres en Montreal y uno en Ohio). De esta forma, Joao Fonseca se despide de los 'majors' esta temporada. Marcando su mejor resultado en la tierra de París siendo capaz de remontar un saco de dos sets a Novak Djokovic y logrando los cuartos de final. Ahí cedió ante el checo Jakub Mensik en tres mangas. El balance del brasileño en los tres Grand Slam disputados en 2026 es de seis victorias y tres derrotas.

articles.title: 'No, not at all': Roger Federer, 45, rules out return to professional tennis
articles.summary: Tennis News: Roger Federer has made it clear that fans should not expect to see him return to professional tennis.The 20-time Grand Slam champion, who retired in 2.
articles.body: Roger Federer has made it clear that fans should not expect to see him return to professional tennis.The 20-time Grand Slam champion, who retired in 2022, is set to play an exhibition match at the US Open but said his appearance in New York is purely for fun and not the start of a comeback.Asked whether he could return to the professional tour, Federer gave a straightforward response.âNo, not at all," Federer said at a press conference, according to Olympics.com.The Swiss great explained that making a comeback would require him to meet several professional obligations, including joining the anti-doping testing pool. More importantly, he said his busy schedule and physical condition make a return unrealistic.âThanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did, so I can clarify in case anybody thought. Anyway, you have to enter the doping pool. There are way too many obstacles. I'm too busy. I'm barely finding time to play any exhos [exhibition matches], so imagine a tour, and the body is done," Federer said.The 45-year-old added that he is comfortable with life away from competitive tennis and now enjoys watching the sport rather than playing it at the highest level.âBut I'm very happy with how I'm feeling. I'm just a fan now, enjoying watching," he added.A new chapter for the Swiss legendFederer last played at the US Open in 2019 before announcing his retirement three years later. He remains the only player, male or female, to win five consecutive US Open titles, achieving the feat from 2004 to 2008.His exhibition appearance comes shortly before another major milestone: his induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Federer was selected in his first year of eligibility and will be inducted on August 29 in Newport, Rhode Island.The Swiss star won 20 Grand Slam singles titles, along with 103 tour-level trophies and Olympic gold and silver medals, before calling time on his legendary career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rafa Jódar vuelve al lugar donde empezó todo: de campeón del júnior del US Open a gran sensación del año
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, de 19 años, disputará por primera vez el grande neoyorquino como profesional
articles.summary: El madrileño, de 19 años, disputará por primera vez el grande neoyorquino como profesional
articles.body: Rafa Jódar cedió en los octavos del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati ante Flavio Cobolli y se tomó un descanso de tenis antes de aterrizar ayer en Nueva York. Este martes, tendrá su primera toma de contacto con las pistas de Flushing Meadows, las mismas que le vieron ganar hace dos temporadas en la prueba júnior del US Open.  Rafa disputará por primera el cuadro de los profesionales y lo hará con el cartel de decimosegundo cabeza de serie. El madrileño se ha convertido en la gran sensación de 2026 gracias a su salto en el ranking. Ha pasado del puesto 165 al 13.  Los registros de Jódar no dejan de asombrar. Se ha convertido en el mejor jugador de la Era Open tras la disputa de 50 partidos. Su balance es de 36 victorias por 14 derrotas. Sólo el argentino José Luis Clerc firmó esos números desde 1968.   Rafa mejora también las cifras del 'Big Three' y Carlos Alcaraz en sus inicios en los torneos Masters 1000, la segunda categoría del tenis después de los Grand Slam. Suma 15 triunfos en 20 partidos.  El tenista del Chamartín realizará hoy su primera sesión preparatoria en el Billie Jean King Tennis Center. Su acompañante será el ruso Karen Khachanov, el 49 de las listas ATP. El entreno está fijado a partir de las 14.30 horas en la ciudad de los rascacielos cuando más aprieta el sol.

articles.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani to Make 1,000 'Affordable' US Open Tickets Available to Local Residents
articles.summary: Amid concerns over the soaring ticket prices for the US Open, local fans in New York City have a new solution.
articles.body:
Amid concerns over the soaring ticket prices for the US Open, local fans in New York City have a new solution.

Per The Athletic's Adam Crafton , New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has secured 1,000 "affordable" tickets for the tournament to distribute to local residents on a first-come, first-served basis.

Crafton reported that Mamdani will announce that $100 tickets will be available for New York City residents to purchase for main-draw matches taking place between Aug. 30 and Sept. 8, running through the quarterfinal stage of the tournament. Tickets will become available on Wednesday at 10 a.m. ET, and buyers must have a certified NYC zip code to be eligible.

"This summer, we have shown again and again that sports belong to the people. From the World Cup to track and field championships, we have opened stadium doors to some of the biggest sporting events in the world so more New Yorkers can enjoy them," Mamdani said in a statement to Crafton. "Today, we are doubling down on that work by making the US Open more affordable for New Yorkers. If the world's best tennis players are coming to our city, New Yorkers should be able to see them play."

It was noted that these particular tickets will not be eligible for resale through Ticketmaster, the tournament's secondary market platform. Ticketmaster has been the source of the price surge, with "grounds passes going for between $240 and $478 as of Tuesday morning, despite the face-value price for the cheapest being $65."

The tickets available for local residents will include ground passes and seats in Arthur Ashe Stadium and Louis Armstrong Stadium. The U.S. Open mixed doubles competition will be held on Tuesday and Wednesday, while the singles main draws will start on Sunday.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Stan Wawrinka thanks tournament after missing out on wildcard
articles.summary: Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.
articles.body:
Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.

The 41-year-old will retire at the end of year and was given a wildcard for this year's Australian Open and Wimbledon, while reaching the French Open main-draw on ranking.

He reached the third round in Melbourne and lost a pair of entertaining first-round matches in Paris and Wimbledon respectively.

The US Open has received some criticism for its decision not to award a wildcard to 2016 champion Wawrinka, who did not enter qualifying despite being inside the cut-off.

The United States Tennis Association (USTA) says it does not comment on wildcard decisions.

Despite not receiving a wildcard, Wawrinka thanked the US Open and the city of New York in a social media post.

"When I first arrived in New York from a small farming village in Switzerland, everything felt too big. The city. The noise. The energy. The crowds. The lights," the Swiss wrote.

"But, year after year, New York slowly became one of my favourite places in the world.

"This city challenged me. It pushed me. It brought something out of me that few places ever could.

"I experienced some of the strongest emotions of my career here. The battles, the late nights, the incredible atmosphere, the love from the crowdâ¦ memories that will stay with me forever.

"Winning the US Open, in the city that never sleeps, will forever be one of the greatest moments of my life."

Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles Published 1 hour ago

Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying Published 2 hours ago

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying

Wawrinka was one of the few players to win major singles trophies during the 'Big Three' era of Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer.

The former world number three won the 2014 Australian Open and 2015 French Open before triumphing at the US Open 10 years ago.

He made 17 appearances in the men's singles in New York since making his main-draw debut in 2005.

Wawrinka's coach, Magnus Norman, wrote on Instagram: "We pushed to play one last Grand Slam at 41 years of age but we just came up short.

"It sure hurts but thanks for all the beautiful memories on and off the court together with you and the team in New York for the past 13 years."

Wildcards are given to players who did not qualify automatically for the tournament by ranking. Wawrinka has fallen outside the top 100 after struggling with injuries and form in recent years.

Switzerland also does not host a Grand Slam, with tournaments reserving reciprocal wildcards for one another.

France's Gael Monfils, who is also retiring this season, was given a wildcard through the French Tennis Federation, which organises the French Open.

Reciprocal wildcards are assigned by the national federations and not the US Open.

The US Open gets under way on Sunday, 30 August at Flushing Meadows.

Other than the reciprocal wildcards the USTA reserves for French and Australian players, the other six wildcards for both the men's and women's singles went to Americans.

The USTA organises and bankrolls the US Open, and would argue it has every right to put its own players first.

But when a charismatic champion like Wawrinka is not given the chance to say a proper farewell to the event he won in 2016, then the sport as a whole suffers.

Home players dominate the list of wildcards at all the Grand Slams, but the Australian Open found space for Stan Wawrinka and Venus Williams, while Wimbledon offered wildcards to Wawrinka, Grigor Dimitrov, Serena Williams and French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

articles.title: Djokovic y Sabalenka duran 49 minutos en el mixto del US Open
articles.standfirst: Siniakova y Patten, los actuales números uno del dobles, remontan un set y ganan en el súper 'tie break'
articles.summary: Siniakova y Patten, los actuales números uno del dobles, remontan un set y ganan en el súper 'tie break'
articles.body: Novak Djokovic y Aryna Sabalenka, que se habían retado a bailar en las escaleras de Roland Garros, se juntaban este martes por primera vez en una pista de tenis para jugar el mixto del US Open. Los primeros cabezas de serie del cuadro, porque cuenta el ranking de individuales, tenían como rivales a los verdaderos números uno. Y es que Henry Patten y Katerina Siniakova son líderes en las respectivas clasificaciones masculina y femenina de dobles en el circuito ATP y WTA. Djokovic y Sabalenka cayeron con estrépito ante Siniakova y Patten, por 1-4, 4-2 y 10-2, en el súper 'tie break' que se alargó 49 minutos. En el deporte y en el tenis gana el que más quiere ganar. Para el serbio y la bielorrusa era una exhibición más, con media entrada en la Arthur Ashe. Para sus verdugos, una victoria que vale 120.000 dólares y que les acerca al botín de un millón. Sabalenka hace tiempo que piensa más en su indumentaria que en la raqueta. Volvió a lucir un colgante que no le aporta nada en el juego, más bien es una molestia.  De hecho, la tenista de Minsk no depende de ella para mantener el liderato de la WTA. Se lo arrebatará Elena Rybakina si alcanza las semifinales.  Siniakova y Patten cayeron después en la antepenúltima ronda con Gael Monfils y Elina Svitolina, por 5-4, 4-5 y 10-8, en 1 hora y 34 minutos. Y es que el galo y la ucraniana, que contrajeron matrimonio en 2021, quieren despedirse a lo grande. Monfils, de 39 años, cuelga la raqueta a finales de temporada.  En la Louis Armstrong, el segundo estadio del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, el dúo checo formado por Jakub Mensik y Karolina Muchova necesitó también de un súper 'tie break' para eliminar a Marcelo Arévalo y Kristina Mladenovic, por 4-1, 2-4 y 10-7. Después se colaron en las semifinales tras superar a los locales Emma Navarro y Tommy Paul, 4-1 y 5-3.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka Lose in 1st Round of Mixed Doubles Bracket at 2026 US Open
articles.summary: One of the top pairs in the US Open mixed doubles competition is already out of the tournament.
articles.body:
One of the top pairs in the US Open mixed doubles competition is already out of the tournament.

No. 1-seeded Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka lost in the first round on Tuesday against the mixed doubles world No. 1 pair of Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten, 1-4, 4-2, 10-2. Siniakova sent an ace past Djokovic for match point.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Djokovic and Sabalenka were originally slated to take on Frances Tiafoe and Leylah Fernandez. However, the lineup had to be shuffled after Tiafoe withdrew from the tournament on Monday due to injury, giving the No. 1 pair a tough test right out of the gate.

Early on, Djokovic and Sabalenka appeared to have the advantage as they cruised to a first-set victory, winning three straight points to close out the frame. After falling behind 2-1 in the second set, Patten and Siniakova stormed back to win the next three points and force a tiebreaker. The duo showed why they're No. 1 in the world with a dominant performance in the deciding set.

"It wasn't looking very good for a while," Patten said after the win, per The Athletic's Lukas Weese . "In this format, we played one game and the first set is gone. We played an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was pretty fun."

Patten and Siniakova didn't have much time to rest before returning to action, as their second-round matchup against the married couple of Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils is already underway at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

articles.title: Asian Games tennis row deepens as AITA rebuts SAI's omission allegation
articles.summary: Tennis News: NEW DELHI: The row over India's tennis squad for the 2026 Asian Games intensified on Tuesday after the All India Tennis Association (AITA) categorical.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The row over India's tennis squad for the 2026 Asian Games intensified on Tuesday after the All India Tennis Association (AITA) categorically rejected claims that it failed to submit the names of excluded players to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).The national federation denied a claim made by Sports Authority of India (SAI) source to news agency PTI that the omitted players â Manas Dhamne, Sahaja Yamalapalli, Vaishnavi Adkar, Vaidehee Chaudhari and Prarthana Thombare â did not feature in the shortlist forwarded by AITA to the IOA, and therefore were absent from the final list considered by the Sports Ministry.However, TimesofIndia.com has accessed the letter dated July 3 which was sent to the IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer where merits of each player, including recent history, was mentioned.AITA stated that Secretary General Sunder Iyer had written to Iyer on July 3, making an "urgent representation seeking review of the exclusion of tennis players from the Indian contingent" and specifically naming Dhamne, Ankita Raina, Yamalapalli, Chaudhari, Adkar and Thombare.In the four-page letter sent on July 3, accessed by TimesofIndia.com, AITA had argued that India should field its strongest possible contingent and maximise medal opportunities across all five tennis events rather than relying solely on uniform ranking criteria.On Monday, as TimesofIndia.com reported, the Sports Ministry had stuck by its selection policy, which requires singles players to be among Asia's top six and doubles players to be inside the continental top-eight over a 12-month evaluation period. The ministry has also maintained that the criteria will not be relaxed despite criticism made by two-time Asian Games medallist Rohan Bopanna.AITA's case for the quartetThe federation's representation highlighted that India had earned multiple strong acceptance-list positions in doubles events.AITA said India had three mixed doubles pairs inside the top-eight accepted entries â Rutuja Bhosale/Yuki Bhambri (seeded No. 2), Ankita Raina/N. Sriram Balaji (No. 5) and Prarthana Thombare/Anirudh Chandrasekar (No. 8). Since each country can enter only two pairs, AITA argued this represented two genuine medal opportunities.It also pointed out that Thombare and Bhosale were positioned at No. 10 on the women's doubles acceptance list, with withdrawals potentially opening the door to the main draw. Excluding established doubles specialists, the federation said, would weaken India's medal prospects.For the singles events, AITA described Yamalapalli as India's highest-ranked women's singles player, praised Adkar's international multi-sport credentials, backed Chaudhari's consistency on tour and termed 18-year-old Dhamne one of India's brightest young prospects whose Asian Games participation would aid both immediate competitiveness and long-term Olympic development.The letter concluded by requesting the IOA to urgently review the exclusions, reassess entries on an event-specific basis and approve all six players to maximise India's medal chances.Ministry steadfast in exclusionsThe controversy erupted after the exclusion of five players from the original 12 member list drew criticism from two-time Asian Games gold medallist Rohan Bopanna.Bopanna had said that "a committee that never stood where they stood has decided their fate on paper, before a ball is struck," adding that denying players the chance to compete was against the principles of building a sporting nation.The Ministry, however, has maintained that recent performances did not establish sufficient medal probability and argued that creating discretionary exceptions for players ranked between 25th and 40th in Asia would undermine administrative integrity and invite litigation from other national sports federations.India's final tennis squad currently includes Sumit Nagal in men's singles, while Yuki Bhambri, Dhakshineswar Suresh, N. Sriram Balaji, Anirudh Chandrasekar, Ankita Raina and Rutuja Bhosale have been selected for the doubles events.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik also reached the last eight after defeating Kristina Mladenovic and Marcelo Arevalo 4-1, 2-4 (10-7).Star-studded mixed doubles eventThe 16-team mixed doubles competition was redesigned last year to attract more leading singles players. It is being held over two days before the singles main draw and uses a faster scoring format designed to limit the physical demands on players.Sabalenka, a two-time defending US Open women's singles champion, and Djokovic, a 24-time Grand Slam winner, were the top seeds based on their combined singles rankings.Despite their early exit, the tournament still features major stars. articles.title: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz exit US Open mixed doubles in quarter-finals; top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka out in first round
articles.summary: Serena Williams, 44, wins her first match since 2022 after her return to tennis in June; mixed doubles defending champions Andrea Vavassori and Sara Errani out in first round; watch the 2026 US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.

The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

With their quarter-final match scheduled immediately afterwards, Williams and Alcaraz ultimately ran out of puff as Bencic and Cobolli triumphed 5-4 4-1, the latter then having hailed their opponents pre-match as "the queen of tennis and the king of now."

The question now is whether Williams will seek an encore performance in women's doubles alongside older sister Venus, having already ruled out a repeat of her singles appearance at Wimbledon.

Djokovic and Sabalenka suffer early exit

Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka were bounced out of the tournament in the opening match on Arthur Ashe, falling to a 1-4 4-2 10-2 ‌defeat to Britain's Henry Patten and Katerina Siniakova.

Djokovic, a ​24-time Grand Slam singles champion, and four-time major winner Sabalenka made a strong start by ​taking the opening set, but doubles specialists Patten and ‌Siniakova hit back to claim the second before dominating the tiebreak ​to secure a place in the quarter-finals.

Siniakova sealed the upset in style with an ace out wide on match ​point, ending the tournament hopes of the ⁠star-studded pairing.

"It wasn't looking very ⁠good for a while, in this format we play one bad game and all ‌of a sudden the first set's gone," Patten said.

"We knew the same could happen in the second, and we played ‌an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was great."

The mixed doubles championship is once again being staged in the week before the singles main draw, after organisers revamped ⁠the format last year to attract more ​leading singles players by reducing the field and ​giving the event a standalone slot on the ​calendar.

The revamped format proved a commercial success in its ⁠debut year, drawing sell-out crowds and attracting many of the sport's biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, ⁠who argued it marginalised established pairings.

Defending champions dumped out in first round

Italian ​duo Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori went on to ​retain the title by defeating Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud in last year's final, but suffered a first-round exit this year.

Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev beat the defending champions 1-4 4-1 11-9 in the opening round, before clinching a semi-final spot with a 4-1 4-5 10-5 victory over Diana Shnaider and Casper Ruud.

They next face Czech pair Karolína Muchova and Jakub Mensik in one of Wednesday's semi-finals, with Bencic and Cobolli facing husband and wife partnership Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina in the other after they edged out Patten and Siniakova in the last eight.

The final two follow the two semis on Wednesday night will resemble a regular match, with traditional sets to six games.

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours live on Sky Sports. The US Open is also live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with NOW and the Sky Sports App .

articles.title: El mixto del US Open se descabeza: Zverev y Townsend, eliminados

articles.summary: Cobolli y Bencic esperan en los cuartos a los ganadores del duelo entre Alcaraz/Serena y Glasspool/Routliffe
articles.body: Alexander Zverev, Aryna Sabalenka y Novak Djokovic, los tenistas con el ranking más alto de los que han jugado hasta el momento el torneo mixto del US Open, han quedado todos eliminados.  Después de que Djokovic se la pegara con Sabalenka, contra Katerina Siniakova y Henry Patten, ha sido Zverev el que se ha despedido este martes al lado de Taylor Townsend. Sus verdugos fueron el italiano Flavio Cobolli y la suiza Belinda Bencic, por 4-2 y 4-2.  Cobolli y Bencic, cuartos cabezas de serie del cuadro, esperan en la antepenúltima ronda a los ganadores del duelo estrella del día. El que medirá a Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams frente a Erin Routlifee y Lloyd Glasspool.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Serena remontan para la historia y pasan a cuartos del mixto del US Open
articles.standfirst: La legendaria pareja levanta dos pelotas de primer set y arrasa después a Glasspool y Routliffe
articles.summary: La legendaria pareja levanta dos pelotas de primer set y arrasa después a Glasspool y Routliffe
articles.body: En su retorno oficial a las pistas, Carlos Alcaraz, con Serena Williams de improvisada acompañante en una instantánea para la historia, ganaron en los octavos del mixto del US Open ante Lloyd Glasspool y Erin Routliffe, por 5-3 y 4-1, en 58 minutos. De esta forma, buscarán a continuación el pase a las semifinales ante Flavio Cobolli y Belinda Bencic.  Cuando Serena se adjudicó en 1998 el título en el mixto del torneo neoyorquino todavía faltaban cinco años para el nacimiento del fenómeno de El Palmar. Cuando Alcaraz nació el 5 de mayo de 2003, en las vitrinas de la pequeña de las Williams ya figuraban cinco títulos de Grand Slam en individuales. Entre Carlitos y Serena se reparten 46 grandes. Lo que pasa es que el deporte vive del presente y la leyenda local colgó la raqueta en 2022 y apenas volvió a la acción en la pasada gira de hierba.  Su objetivo de jugar en casa delante de sus hijas, Olympia y Adira River, ya lo ha logrado. Alcaraz, por su parte, se vistió de corto 133 días después de la lesión en la muñeca derecha de Barcelona y le falta rodaje aunque le sobran ganas de volver a ganar.  A Routliffe y Glasspool, dos exnúmeros uno en la modalidad de dobles, que venían rodados tras pasar la previa del lunes y coronarse en Washington, les entró el miedo escénico cuando tenían el partido controlado. Suele pasar cuando juegas contra leyendas.  Era la segunda campaña seguida que Alcaraz se apuntaba al mixto en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos. En su anterior experiencia había cedido en el debut contra Jessica Pegula y Jack Draper. A diferencia del año pasado, donde reservó su equipación Nike para el estreno en la competición individual, Alcaraz lució ya en el mixto los diseños preparados en exclusiva por la multinacional americana. Y es que para él era muy especial juntarse a mitad de pista con Serena. No había mayor ni mejor escaparate. La elástica es un homenaje al popular baloncesto estadounidense. A Carlitos volvió a acompañarle su inseparable malla en el brazo derecho. El tenista español venía de ejercitarse durante una hora con Arthur Fils, flamante campeón el domingo del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati. El murciano perdió su primer turno de saque, con una doble falta en el primer punto. La falta de competición se notaba. Routliffe y Glasspool cargaban más el juego hacia Serena y se equivocaron en la táctica.  Del 3-1 en contra para los favoritos del público se pasó al 5-3 a favor tras salvar dos pelotas de primer set en el sexto juego cuando estaba sacando Glasspool. Con servicios de Serena a 193 kilómetros por hora es más sencillo remontar. Una derecha demoledora de Alcaraz dio la primera ventaja en el marcador.   Hasta siete juegos seguidos llegaron a encadenar el español y la estadounidense, que se estaba convirtiendo en la gran protagonista de la tarde. Glasspool y Routliffe cerraron la sangría salvando las dos primeras bolas de eliminación. Pero con 3-1 la diferencia era demasiado grande para soñar en la remontada. "Estaba nervioso por estar al lado de Serena. Se ha notado con la doble falta del primer punto", explicaba Carlitos a la conclusión.

images.caption: Serena remata ante la presencia de Alcaraz. Yuki Iwamura

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz's Highlights and Top Stats from Return in US Open Mixed Doubles
articles.summary: A tennis legend and a legend in the making teamed up at the US Open in mixed doubles on Tuesday.
articles.body:
A tennis legend and a legend in the making teamed up at the US Open in mixed doubles on Tuesday.

Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz opened up the tournament with a comeback win against Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool in the first round. Williams and Alcaraz won the match 5-3, 4-1.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Routliffe and Glaspool had the early edge in Tuesday's match, taking a 2-0 lead and then a 3-1 lead in the first set, but Williams and Alcaraz scored their first break of the match to tie things up at 3-3. They took a 4-3 lead after surviving two set points.

The pair then secured the set 5-3 after winning their second break. From there, it was a mostly dominant showing as Routliffe and Glaspool won just one of the final eight games of the match.

Tuesday marked Williams' first appearance at Arthur Ashe Stadium since 2022. She and Alcaraz received a wild-card entry into the mixed doubles portion of the U.S. Open.

Though Williams hasn't technically retired, she has been mostly inactive in competitive tennis since August 2022, when she told Vogue that she would be "evolving away from tennis" to focus on "other things that are important to me."

However, she's used the summer to ramp back into tennis shape, playing in the HSBC Championships in June before playing in four other tournaments ahead of the U.S. Open.

Alcaraz is likewise making a comeback, albeit not quite to the extent of Williams. The star missed the last four months of action due to a wrist injury, forcing him to sit out the French Open and Wimbledon.

Now having won in their first-round matchup, Williams and Alcaraz will take on the fourth-seeded pairing of Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.

articles.title: US Open 2026 qualifying results: Harriet Dart and Fran Jones win opening matches
articles.summary: Britons Harriet Dart and Fran Jones both make winning starts in their bids to reach the US Open singles main draw.
articles.body:
Britons Harriet Dart and Fran Jones both made winning starts to their bids to reach the US Open singles main draw.

Dart, who has twice reached the US Open second round, came through 6-0 6-7 (1-7) 6-1 against Jordyn Hazelitt in the first round of qualifying in New York.

She will face another American 16-year-old, Kristina Penickova, next.

Jones, who qualified for the US Open for the first time last year, will face Germany's Mona Barthel after winning 6-3 6-4 against Italy's Nuria Brancaccio.

But Jodie Burrage lost to Spain's Guiomar Maristany 7-6 (7-1) 6-4, while Henry Searle was beaten 6-1 6-2 by American 16-year-old Michael Antonius in the men's event.

Antonius will face former US Open finalist Kei Nishikori in the second qualifying round, after the Japanese 36-year-old battled to a 6-1 2-6 6-2 win over Austrian Sebastian Ofner.

Former US Open semi-finalist Grigor Dimitrov will face Kazakhstan's Timofey Skatov in his second qualifying match after dismissing Italy's Lorenzo Giustino 6-0 6-3.

In the women's draw, 2019 US Open winner Bianca Andreescu progressed with a 6-1 6-2 win against Dutch player Eva Vedder.

Heather Watson resumes her qualifying campaign with a second-round match against Spain's Angela Fita Boluda on Wednesday.

In the men's draw, Britons Jacob Fearnley, Toby Samuel, Billy Harris, Harry Wendelken and Jack Pinnington Jones all return to action seeking to move one win away from the Flushing Meadows main draw.

Players must come through three rounds of qualifying to reach the singles main draw, which gets under way on Sunday.

Elsewhere, Britain's Arthur Fery warmed up for the US Open with a 6-1 7-5 victory over Cruz Hewitt at the Winston-Salem Open.

Fery, playing just his third match since his stunning run to the Wimbledon semi-finals, came back from 4-1 down in the second set to advance.

The fourth seed will play either Czech Tomas Machac or Dutch qualifier Mees Rottgering next.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Serena ceden en cuartos del mixto ante Cobolli y Bencic
articles.standfirst: El murciano y la estadounidense pagan la inactividad y la falta de descanso entre partidos
articles.summary: El murciano y la estadounidense pagan la inactividad y la falta de descanso entre partidos
articles.body: Mientras Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams remontaban su partido de octavos del cuadro mixto del US Open ante Lloyd Glasspool y Erin Routliffe, Flavio Cobolli y Belinda Bencic tuvieron una hora de descanso. Ese margen les dio una chispa que les faltó a Alcaraz y la Williams después en el duelo con el italiano y la suiza. Estos últimos se impusieron en los cuartos, por 5-4(4) y 4-1, en 55 minutos.  A Serena, de 44 años y que se retiró en 2022 para volver esporádicamente a jugar varios partidos en 2026, se le notó la edad y su inactividad. Toda la brillantez y la potencia que había demostrado la estadounidense en el debut se había tornado en errores no forzados.  Carlitos, que no jugaba desde el 14 de abril, hacía lo que podía. Cobolli y Bencic, muy bien compenetrados, pasaron a semifinales. Allí se encontrarán al matrimonio formado por Gael Monfils y Elina Svitolina.   El campeón de siete grandes se concentrará ahora en la competición individual. Este jueves aparecerá en el cuadro como segundo cabeza de serie por la ausencia de Jannik Sinner. Su debut será entre el 30 de agosto y el 1 de septiembre.

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz drop quarterfinal match after opening-round win in US Open mixed doubles
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up on Tuesday in a US Open return that was significant for both.
articles.body:
Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up Tuesday in mixed doubles for a US Open return that was significant for both.

They delivered with a comeback, 5-3, 4-1 win over mixed doubles specialists Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool in first-round play, much to the delight of a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd that showed up to cheer on the tennis superstars.

They then fell in the quarterfinals to the fourth-seeded team of Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli, 5-4 (7-4), 4-1.

Serena, Alcaraz delight US Open crowd with first-round win

In the first round, Routliffe and Glasspool broke Alcaraz's first serve and took 2-0 and 3-1 leads in the first set. Sets on Tuesday were played to four games.

Then, trailing 3-2 with the first set on the line, Williams and Alcaraz scored their first break of the match to tie the set at 3-3. They survived two set points to keep the set alive. Williams then delivered with a pair of aces on her serve to take a 4-3 lead.

Four unreturned serves (two were aces) in one game from Serena Williams. That's what she does. pic.twitter.com/4P0M24bRCr — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

Four unreturned serves (two were aces) in one game from Serena Williams. That's what she does. pic.twitter.com/4P0M24bRCr

With a chance to set up game point on their next serve, Williams delivered a fiery forehand winner off a Routliffe serve.

Serena Williams extended grunt return winner‼️ pic.twitter.com/3FgSeUmIR8 — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

Serena Williams extended grunt return winner‼️ pic.twitter.com/3FgSeUmIR8

Williams and Alcaraz followed through with their second break to secure the set, 5-3. They were in control from there. Routliffe and Glasspool won just one of the final eight games as Williams and Alcaraz put on a show for the supportive New York crowd.

"It's always such an amazing place to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said in her post-match interview. "It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."

Just minutes after their first-round win, Williams and Alcaraz took the Arthur Ashe Stadium court again in the quarterfinals. There, Bencic and Cobolli proved to be a significantly tougher test.

The two teams played to a tiebreak in the first set that Bencic and Cobolli won, 7-4. Williams hit a would-be winner long that allowed Bencic and Cobolli to extend their tiebreak lead to 6-4. Cobolli then sealed the first-set win with an ace.

Sealed with an ace 💥 Bencic/Cobolli take the first set 5-4 vs Williams/Alcaraz! pic.twitter.com/2i9LFajyNt — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

Sealed with an ace 💥 Bencic/Cobolli take the first set 5-4 vs Williams/Alcaraz! pic.twitter.com/2i9LFajyNt

Much like Williams and Alcaraz in their first match, Bencic and Cobolli were in control in the second set of the quarterfinals.

A Cobolli return forced a mishit by Alcaraz on game point in the fourth game, allowing Bencic and Cobolli to break and serve for the match, leading 3-1. Cobolli then delivered on his serve to secure the win and their place in the semifinals.

Perfect day at the office 🫡 Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli end the run of Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz 5-4, 4-1 to reach the semifinals! pic.twitter.com/S9ymVwYOoz — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

Perfect day at the office 🫡 Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli end the run of Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz 5-4, 4-1 to reach the semifinals! pic.twitter.com/S9ymVwYOoz

The win marked the fourth won set in four sets played for Bencic and Cobolli after they swept Taylor Townsend and Alexander Zverev earlier Tuesday. They'll take on Elina Svitolina and Gaël Monfils in the semifinals on Wednesday.

A comeback for both Williams and Alcaraz

For Williams, the match was her first at Arthur Ashe Stadium since her final pre-retirement singles match in 2022. She was back at the US Open on Tuesday competing with one of the biggest stars in the game in Alcaraz as part of a limited comeback to tennis. She will not play in the women's singles bracket.

Williams began her comeback in the spring that included a first-round singles loss at Wimbledon to Maya Joint. She's since played doubles with her sister, Venus at the Cincinnati Open, where they lost in three sets in the first round to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

U.S. Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka lose first match, fall to top-ranked mixed doubles team

US Open 2026: How scheduling and purse changes lured tennis' biggest stars to mixed doubles event

Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz teaming up in 2026 US Open mixed doubles tournament

For Alcaraz, the match marked his return to competitive tennis for the first time since he suffered a wrist injury in April that sidelined him for Wimbledon and the French Open. Alcaraz was initially listed in the field for the Cincinnati Open earlier in August, but he withdrew amid the lingering injury.

His nerves were apparent on the court as he started the first-round match with a double fault, but he settled into his game from there.

"I was out for four months and a half, almost five months," Alcaraz said after the first-round win. "I almost forget how it feels stepping on the court once again."

Now Alcaraz is back for the final Grand Slam of the year. Despite his rust, the two-time and reigning US Open champion is the favorite to win the men's singles title in a field that doesn't feature injured World No. 1 Jannik Sinner .

images.caption: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 25: Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams high five during a mixed doubles match during Fan Week as part of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 in Flushing, NY. (Photo by Darren Carroll/USTA via Getty Images) (Darren Carroll via Getty Images)

articles.title: US Open 2026: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz return in mixed doubles
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz were among the star double-acts in New York as the US Open mixed doubles competition got under way on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to.

That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.

The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.

But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.

Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.

The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.

The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.

Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.

Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."

Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.

However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying Published 5 hours ago

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying

Wawrinka 'grateful' despite no US Open wildcard Published 10 hours ago

Wawrinka 'grateful' despite no US Open wildcard

Returning Alcaraz 'almost forgot how this feels'

While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.

The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.

"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.

"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.

"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."

For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.

"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.

"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."

The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.

The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.

Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.

Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.

Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.

"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."

The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.

It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.

'The sort of semi-final line-up organisers envisaged'

Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.

With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.

Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.

But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.

The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.

This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz 1st-Round Win Highlights US Open Mixed Doubles Day 1 Bracket Results
articles.summary: The mixed doubles tournament at the U.S. Open kicked off on Tuesday, with some big names—including Novak Djokovic, Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz—all in action.
articles.body:
The mixed doubles tournament at the U.S. Open kicked off on Tuesday, with some big names—including Novak Djokovic, Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz—all in action.

Here's a look at the day's results and best highlights.

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli def. Alexander Zverev/Taylor Townsend, 4-2, 4-2

Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul def. Amanda Anisimova/Learner Tien, 5(4)-3(1), 4-2

Katerina Siniakova/Henry Patten def. Aryna Sabalenka/Novak Djokovic, 1-4, 4-2, 1-1

Karlina Muchova/Jakub Mensik def. Kristina Mladenovic/Marcelo Arevalo, 4-1, 2-4, 1-0

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils def. Alexandra Eala/Felix Auger-Aliassime, 4-1, 4-1

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev def. Andrea Vavassori/Sara Errani, 1-4, 4-1, 1-0

Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud def. Jessica Pegula/Taylor Fritz, 4-2, 4-1

Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz def. Erin Routliffe/Lloyd Glasspool, 5-3, 4-1

Karlina Muchova/Jakub Mensik def. Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul, 4-1, 4-3

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils def. Katerina Siniakova/Henry Patten 5-4, 4-5, 1-0

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli def. Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz, 5-4, 4-1

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev def. Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud, 4-1, 4-5, 10-5

The duo of Vavassori and Errani falling in the first round was a major result, given they were the reigning U.S. Open mixed doubles champions.

It also wasn't a great day for the top seeds. The No. 1 seed, Sabalenka and Djokovic, fell in the first round. So did the No. 2 seed (Fritz and Pegula) and No. 3 seed (Anisimova and Tien).

The No. 4 seed Bencic and Cobolli is now the favorites, especially after eliminating the iconic duo of Williams and Alcaraz in the quarterfinals.

"I don't know how I landed on this court to play Carlos and Serena," Bencic said after the match. "It was an honor to play."

Alcaraz, meanwhile, certainly had some rust to shake off after being out of action since April.

"I think everybody could see: I double-faulted on the first point," he said. "I was really, really nervous. I was out for four months... I almost forget how it feels."

Bencic and Cobolli will now face Svitolina and Monfils in the semifinals, while the other match will pit Muchova and Mensik against Andreeva and Rublev.

articles.title: Haters of fashion attack Aryna Sabalenka with 'streetwalker' insult simply because she wore fishnet at US Open
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's bold mesh dress at the US Open sparked fierce backlash, but the tennis star had a defiant response ready for her fashion critics.
articles.body: Good luck being a leader and trying something new, especially when it comes to fashion. I've said it before, I'm not an expert nor will I pretend to be one. That doesn’t mean there aren't others more than willing to pretend. There are, and they've set their sights on Aryna Sabalenka. She dared to show up to the US Open in what haters of fashion have labeled a fishnet dress. The adults out there may refer to it, correctly, as a mesh dress. I’d like to take a moment to thank Dua Lipa for several lessons in fashion, lessons that, let the record show, I retained despite being reluctantly dragged into them. NAOMI OSAKA'S ALL-BLACK FRENCH OPEN OUTFIT RIVALS HER JELLYFISH-INSPIRED LOOK FROM THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN It made it easier to spot what unfolded at Arthur Ashe Stadium. Sabalenka was on the court with her mixed doubles partner Novak Djokovic taking on Kateřina Siniaková and Henry Patten. She and Djokovic ended up losing the match. While dealing with the top-ranked in mixed doubles, the self-appointed fashion experts went on the attack. Who knew a little mesh would cause such a reaction? "How about that - Sabalenka leading the parade of streetwalker chic at the US Open with fishnet over shorts and a sports bra," one of the critics wrote. "Why does New York bring out all the trashy-ness?" SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS OVER NEW BROADCASTING GUIDELINES THAT DISCOURAGE 'SEXUALIZED' SHOTS OF FEMALE ATHLETES "Sabalenka ’s maximalist jewellery with those multicoloured stones set in gold clashes badly with her US open kit. Looks a mess imo," said another. One called it a "clown kit" and wrote in disbelief, "this sabalenka clown kit can’t be actually real." These attacks on her fashion didn’t catch Aryna Sabalenka by surprise. She knew they were coming. She was prepared for it after rolling out the new Nike looks a few weeks ago. "I love my outfit. If someone doesn't like it, it's okay. You cannot impress everyone with your outfits," she said earlier this month. "That's why I like fashion because there is room for whatever, basically." OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Take that, haters. Nice try. A mesh dress on top of shorts and a sports bra doesn't help you win your match. It also doesn't make you the leader of an imaginary "parade of streetwalker chic" either. I can't believe that had to be pointed out and that I had to be the one to do it. Yet here we are.

articles.title: Serena Williams Reacts to US Open Return in Video After Mixed Doubles with Carlos Alcaraz
articles.summary: Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2022 to compete alongside Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles at the U.S. Open.
articles.body:
Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2022 to compete alongside Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles at the U.S. Open.

She and Alcaraz started things off with a win over Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool, and the tennis legend was thrilled to be back on the court.

"I never expected to be back on this court, so it was just a really cool moment," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

Williams has been out of action for much of the last four years but got a bit of a warm-up this summer as she participated in various tournaments. Despite so much time off, she looked more than comfortable alongside Alcaraz.

Alcaraz has also been away for a significant amount of time, missing the last four months with a wrist injury. Playing alongside an all-time great was nerve-wracking, but ultimately helped him ease back into it.

"I was really nervous playing alongside Serena," Alcaraz said. "... She made it really easy for me just to try to enjoy it, go for it every time."

Following the win in the opening round, Williams and Alcaraz lost to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarterfinals.

articles.title: Roger Federer Plays at US Open with John McEnroe, Andy Roddick, Agassi, Top Moments & Highlights
articles.summary: For one night, a legend was back on the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2019.
articles.body:
For one night, a legend was back on the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2019.

Roger Federer participated in a special exhibition event on Tuesday ahead of the start of the main draw at this year's U.S. Open. The 20-time Grand Slam champion was joined by Andy Roddick, John McEnroe and Andre Agassi for the celebratory matches.

Federer faced Roddick in a set of singles competition before teaming with McEnroe to go against Roddick and Agassi.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Perhaps the first hint at the magnitude of the night was the reaction Federer received before a coin toss that featured another notable name:

Once the tennis started, it was clear Federer hadn't lost his skills.

He cruised to a 6-3 victory over Roddick behind a powerful serve and some of his famous backhands:

It was an impressive showing considering how long he has been away from the game.

"I haven't played a singles set in, I don't know, (Hubert) Hurkacz at Wimbledon maybe, so it's been five years," Federer said Monday, per Brian Mahoney of the Associated Press. "I don't know how it's going to go tomorrow. So there is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful moments."

The fans were happy to remember those beautiful moments Tuesday as they watched him play on the same court he enjoyed so much success on during the peak of his career.

Federer won five consecutive U.S. Open men's singles titles from 2004 through 2008. He also reached the final again in 2009 and 2015 and was a fan favorite for much of his run.

Those moments all came during his singles career, but he also mixed it up in the doubles match that was filled with notable names in the second half of Tuesday's performance.

He and McEnroe defeated Roddick and Agassi, 7-5, in a match that let all four of them show off their skills at various times.

While it was notable to see the 45-year-old back on the court, he also was quick to shut down any rumors about a potential comeback.

"No, no, no, no. No, not at all," Federer said ahead of the event. "Thanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought."

Tuesday was just the start of what figures to be a celebratory week for the all-time great.

He is also the headliner of the 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame class and will be enshrined Saturday in Newport, Rhode Island.

articles.title: Who is Andy Roddick's wife? Meet Brooklyn Decker, the actress and model married to the tennis legend
articles.summary: International Sports News: Andy Roddick won a US Open title in 2003 and spent years ranked No. 1 in the world, but his personal life has drawn nearly as much attention as his te.
articles.body: Andy Roddick won a US Open title in 2003 and spent years ranked No. 1 in the world, but his personal life has drawn nearly as much attention as his tennis career. His wife, Brooklyn Decker, is a familiar name in both fashion and Hollywood. The couple met in 2007, got engaged in 2008, and wed on April 17, 2009. They have been together for nearly two decades now, raising two kids and building a life far removed from the tennis circuit. Here is everything worth knowing about who Brooklyn Decker is and how their relationship took shape.How did Andy Roddick and Brooklyn Decker meet?The origin story is less romantic dinner, more cold DM. Andy Roddick first saw Decker hosting a Sports Illustrated football show online. He reached out to her, and she eventually agreed to connect. What followed moved fast. They dated for about a year before he proposed, and the two got engaged in March 2008.Roddick himself admitted the whole thing caught him off guard. "I went from, 'I don't think I'm gonna get in a serious relationship forever,' and then we were engaged in, like, six months. And then we really got to know each other," he told GQ in 2023.They married at Roddick's private home in Austin, Texas. Decker wore a Vera Wang gown for the evening ceremony, and Elton John performed for the couple and their guests at the celebration that followed. She was 21 at the time; Roddick was 26.Balancing the marriage was not always straightforward. Roddick was still an active player, traveling for tournaments, while Decker had her own demanding schedule. He later said the engagement itself was what held them together through those stretches apart. "If we hadn't actually made that commitment, I don't know that we would get through that."They have two children together. Son Hank was born in October 2015, and daughter Stevie arrived in 2017. Decker has described their current family dynamic with characteristic humor. "Marriage does become hilariously transactional," she told Us Weekly. "You're like, 'I've got the kids, you go buy the tampons, go get the diapers.' It's very like making a game plan for a football game."Who is Brooklyn Decker beyond her marriage to Andy Roddick?Most people first encountered Brooklyn Decker through a magazine cover. She appeared in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue starting in 2006 before landing the cover of the 2010 edition, one of the most visible spots in the modeling world at the time. That visibility opened doors in Hollywood.Her film debut came in 2011 with Just Go with It alongside Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston. She followed that with roles in Battleship and What to Expect When You're Expecting, but her most sustained acting work came on the small screen. In 2015, she took on the role of Mallory Hanson in the Netflix series Grace and Frankie, playing the daughter of Jane Fonda's character. The role ran for 28 episodes across all seven seasons, ending in 2022.Decker has spoken openly about how the transition from modeling to acting was a deliberate choice, not a fallback. "The Sports Illustrated cover was the last thing I shot. I told my agent, 'I don't want to be a model anymore. I really want to do movies.'"Beyond the screen, she co-created a digital wardrobe app called Finery, which was later acquired by Stitch Fix. She also serves as a global ambassador for the Special Olympics.Roddick's retirement from tennis in 2012 changed the texture of their family life considerably. As Decker put it during a 2017 Tennis Channel interview: "He's an unbelievable dad, incredibly hands-on. I feel so thankful that it happened after he retired, because he's here every day with them."In April 2026, the couple marked their 17th wedding anniversary. Decker posted a photo on Instagram of the two in colonial costumes, joking that the years have felt much longer than they actually have. Fitting for a couple that has, in many ways, built something more interesting than either of their careers alone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Roger Federer rolls back years to beat Andy Roddick in exhibition at US Open
articles.summary: New York fans enjoyed a vintage Federer singles win before the 20-time Grand Slam champion teamed up with John McEnroe to beat Andy Roddick and Andre Agassi; watch the 2026 US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The event, billed as "An Icon Returns to New York", packed the stands with fans eager to watch the 45-year-old Swiss star face Andy Roddick, who is soon to turn 44, in a prime-time exhibition.

Federer defeated Roddick in an opening singles match before teaming up with John McEnroe to win a doubles exhibition against Roddick and Andre Agassi.

Federer, a 20-time Grand Slam champion, returned to the court at the US Open for the first time since 2019.

The Swiss legend won five consecutive US Open men's singles titles between 2004 and 2008, tying Pete Sampras and Jimmy Connors for the most in the Open era.

"It's great to be back in New York," Federer said. "It's incredible.

"I have incredible memories of this court, the fans here and the city. In 2004 and 2005, that's when it all started here, my love for New York, with the victories here."

He added: "I fell in love with this city and this court from day one.

"I believe my first time on Centre Court was against Andre [Agassi] in 2001. He smashed me 6-1, 6-2, 6-4. I had no shot. I was like, 'Okay, not so easy, not so fast, Roger.'"

Watch the US Open live from August 30 on Sky Sports Tennis. Stream tennis with NOW and the Sky Sports App .

articles.title: “Whatever I Feel Doesn’t Matter”- Andy Roddick Reacts as American Tennis Eyes US Open History
articles.summary: It has been 23 years since Andy Roddick won his US Open title, and the country is still in search of its next men’s Grand Slam champion. Roddick was present...
articles.body:
It has been 23 years since Andy Roddick won his US Open title, and the country is still in search of its next men's Grand Slam champion. Roddick was present at Arthur Ashe on Tuesday and, along with another great, Andre Agassi, expressed hope that the American men's contingent would end the long wait.

"Well whatever I feel doesn't matter as much as the support they get inside of the building," said Roddick after his doubles match against Roger Federer and John McEnroe. "You all will play a big part in doing it, so I hope it happens and that you all will help them along the way."

With the likes of Jannik Sinner out with an injury, and with Carlos Alcaraz coming back after a long injury layoff, the chances for an American champion at this year's US Open are high. Of the 32 seeds in the men's draw, six are American, with the likes of Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz being the best bets for the title for the American men.

Not only Roddick, but even Agassi was optimistic about the chances of his compatriots at the Flushing Meadows over the next two weeks.

There's real momentum building around the American men at the US Open right now. Subscribe for more interesting stories.

"I think we have a great group of Americans right now and this might just be the two weeks one of them show that it can be get done," said Agassi during the on-court interview.

The two American legends teamed up against the pair of Federer and McEnroe in an exhibition event which celebrated the Swiss player's comeback on Arthur Ashe after seven years. It was a loss for the all-American team, and Roddick went on to lose his singles match against Federer as well, but will hope for better American fortunes for the top-ranked American players in the men's draw.

Up until a couple of years ago, Roddick was not only the last American player to win a Slam, but also the last American player to reach a Slam final at the 2009 Wimbledon. However, the latter record was taken from Roddick's name, with Taylor Fritz reaching the US Open final in 2024.

The hard-court warm-up events before the US Open have seen decent results for some American players, increasing their chances heading into Flushing Meadows next week. Taylor Fritz won the title in Washington, with Ben Shelton in supreme form at the Canadian Open, successfully defending his title. Even Frances Tiafoe had a great warm-up for New York, reaching the final of the Cincinnati Open.

However, this is not the first time that Roddick has had bullish expectations from his compatriots at a Grand Slam. Before Wimbledon, the former American pro was confident that one of the American players would reach the semifinals, with Alcaraz not at SW19. Roddick's confidence was understandable: Tiafoe and Shelton had both won grass-court titles before Wimbledon, beating Fritz in the respective finals.

But Shelton struggled to meet expectations, losing in the first round, whereas Tiafoe gave away several opportunities to take the lead and lost in the third round. Fritz was the only one who went deep but lost to Alexander Zverev in the quarterfinals, with the American struggling with knee injuries.

With the American crowd behind them, one can expect that the top American players will have a better time at Flushing Meadows. All three of the American favorites have had their best Slam moments at the US Open, which is where Roddick and Agassi hope the American men can finally end the Grand Slam drought.
